title: French Lentil Soup
subtitle: Puy lentils with carrots, celery, and crème fraîche
excerpt: Puy lentils simmered with vegetables, bay, and thyme in a well-seasoned stock. Partially blended so it keeps some texture, then finished with a spoonful of crème fraîche and a drizzle of good olive oil.

recipe.sourceNotes: Puy lentils, from the Auvergne region of France, hold their shape better than red lentils and have a firmer, slightly peppery flavour. They are used widely in French peasant cooking and appear in soups, salads, and as a bed for duck confit. The key advantage over red lentils for soup is that they can be partially blended: blend a third of the soup and stir it back in to get a thick, textured result without being fully puréed.

recipeTools.notes: A 4-litre pot for the lentils and stock.

content.text: Puy lentils do not need soaking. Rinse them, pick out any grit, and add directly to the pot. The partial blend at the end is optional: you can serve the soup fully textured or fully smooth depending on preference. Season only after cooking: salt added early can toughen the lentil skins.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed lentils, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs. Pour in the hot stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 25 to 30 minutes until the lentils are tender but still holding their shape.
Remove the bay leaves and thyme stalks. For a thicker soup, scoop out a third of the soup, blend it smooth, and stir it back in. Add the red wine vinegar. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls. Add a spoonful of crème fraîche and a drizzle of olive oil to each bowl.
